subject: Economics
description: Covers Primary/Tertiary sectors and Disguised unemployment.

questions.stem: In the context of the Indian economy, which sector is referred to as the 'Primary Sector'?

options.option_text: Agriculture and allied activities
Manufacturing and Industries
Services like IT and Banking
High-level Research and Development

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Primary Sector involves the direct extraction or harvesting of natural resources from the earth. This includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining. It forms the base for all other products.
DECOY BUSTING: Manufacturing is the Secondary Sector. Services (banking, transport) form the Tertiary Sector. Research & Development is often classed as the Quaternary Sector.
EXAM INSIGHT: Even though the Primary Sector contributes the LEAST to India's GDP (around 18-20%), it famously employs the LARGEST portion of the Indian workforce (around 45%), highlighting a massive productivity/underemployment issue in agriculture.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Which of the following activities falls under the 'Tertiary Sector' of the economy?

options.option_text: Banking and Insurance
Textile manufacturing
Mining of iron ore
Dairy farming

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Tertiary Sector is the service sector. It doesn't produce physical goods; instead, it provides services that support the primary and secondary sectors and the general population. Banking, insurance, transport, trade, healthcare, and education all fall under this sector.
DECOY BUSTING: Textile manufacturing is Secondary (processing raw materials). Mining and dairy farming are Primary (extracting from nature).
EXAM INSIGHT: The Tertiary sector is the undisputed backbone of the modern Indian economy, contributing over 50% to the total GDP, largely driven by the IT/BPO boom since the 1990s.

questions.stem: The phenomenon of 'Disguised Unemployment' is most commonly observed in which sector of the Indian economy?

options.option_text: Agriculture
Information Technology
Manufacturing
Banking

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Disguised unemployment occurs when more people are employed in a job than are actually required to do it. If some workers are removed, total production does not decrease because their marginal productivity is zero. In India, this is rampant in agriculture, where an entire family of 6 might work on a small farm that only really needs 2 people to tend it.
DECOY BUSTING: IT, Manufacturing, and Banking usually suffer from 'Cyclical' unemployment (due to recessions) or 'Structural' unemployment (due to changing skills), but rarely disguised unemployment as private companies won't pay extra unneeded workers.
EXAM INSIGHT: Another common type of rural unemployment is 'Seasonal Unemployment', where farmers have no work during the off-season (months when no crops are sown or harvested).

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST defines a worker belonging to the 'Organised Sector' as opposed to the 'Unorganised Sector' in India?

options.option_text: Employed in agriculture, forestry, or fishing activities
Works in a registered enterprise with statutory benefits like PF and ESI
Earns income exclusively through self-employment or own-account work
Works in industries with annual turnover above a fixed crore threshold

questions.explanation: The Organised Sector comprises enterprises registered under government laws and required to follow rules on working hours, wages, and benefits like Provident Fund (PF) and Employee State Insurance (ESI). Option D is a common confusion — no single turnover threshold defines organised vs unorganised; registration and labour-law compliance are the defining criteria.

questions.stem: In the standard three-sector model of an economy, the activity of 'mining coal from underground reserves' is classified under which sector?

options.option_text: Secondary sector — it transforms extracted materials through processing
Tertiary sector — it provides essential energy services to industries
Primary sector — it involves direct extraction of resources from earth
Quaternary sector — it uses advanced geological and scientific knowledge

questions.explanation: Mining is a Primary Sector activity because it involves direct extraction of natural resources without transforming them. Students frequently misclassify it as Secondary (manufacturing) due to its industrial appearance. The Secondary Sector involves processing or transformation of raw materials, not mere extraction. Tertiary covers services; Quaternary covers knowledge-based work.

questions.stem: Under India's National Industrial Classification (NIC), which of the following activities is classified under the Secondary Sector in national income accounting?

options.option_text: Transport and logistics services for moving finished goods to markets
Electricity generation from coal-fired thermal power plants
Wholesale trade of agricultural commodities in regulated mandis
Financial intermediation services provided by commercial banks

questions.explanation: Electricity generation is classified under the Secondary Sector (utilities/manufacturing) in national accounts because it involves transformation of fuel/energy into a new product — electricity. Transport and wholesale trade are Tertiary sector activities. Students commonly misclassify power generation as a service (Tertiary), but NIC 2008 groups it under 'Electricity, gas, steam and air conditioning supply' — an industrial division.

questions.stem: India's rapid expansion of IT and BPO industries in the 1990s, where the services sector surpassed manufacturing in GDP share without a corresponding industrial revolution, is referred to by economists as?

options.option_text: Secondary sector displacement driven by low-cost industrial labour
Balanced structural transformation with primary sector declining evenly
Service-led growth or premature tertiarisation bypassing industrialisation
Import substitution industrialisation transitioning to export orientation

questions.explanation: India's services sector grew to over 55% of GDP without manufacturing ever dominating — unlike the classic Lewis Model trajectory where economies industrialise before tertiaryising. Economists call this 'premature tertiarisation' or service-led growth. Option D (import substitution) refers to a trade policy framework, not a description of sectoral structure.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the 'Quaternary Sector', a concept added beyond the traditional three-sector model of the economy?

options.option_text: Industries producing capital goods for use in manufacturing units
Knowledge-based services like research, education, and IT consulting
Export-oriented services that earn significant foreign exchange revenues
Financial services including banking, insurance, and capital markets

questions.explanation: The Quaternary Sector specifically refers to knowledge-intensive intellectual activities such as R&D, information technology, education, and consulting. It is distinct from the broader Tertiary sector. Financial services (Option D) are Tertiary, not Quaternary. Export-orientation (Option C) is a trade characteristic, not a sectoral definition. This concept is increasingly tested in SSC CGL and banking exams.

questions.stem: Under the System of National Accounts (SNA 2008), which of the following is explicitly included within the GDP production boundary even though no cash transaction occurs?

options.option_text: Unpaid household services like cooking and cleaning done by family members
Imputed rent for owner-occupied housing estimated at prevailing market rates
Voluntary services rendered to registered non-profit charitable bodies
Informal barter exchanges between neighbours with no monetary payment involved

questions.explanation: SNA 2008 explicitly includes imputed rent for owner-occupied housing — the owner is treated as both landlord and tenant, and a market rental value is estimated and counted in GDP. This is one of the few non-cash activities inside the production boundary. Unpaid domestic work (Option A) is explicitly excluded despite its economic value — a longstanding criticism of GDP as a welfare measure. Volunteer work (Option C) is also excluded unless it is production for sale.

questions.stem: The NCEUS (Arjun Sengupta Committee) drew a key distinction between the 'Unorganised Sector' and the 'Informal Economy'. Which option correctly captures this distinction?

options.option_text: Unorganised Sector covers farm workers only; Informal Economy covers all rural labour
Informal Economy includes informal workers employed in both organised and unorganised enterprises
Unorganised Sector means unregistered firms; Informal Economy means unregistered workers only
Informal Economy refers solely to self-employed and own-account workers in rural India

questions.explanation: The NCEUS made a critical distinction: the 'Unorganised Sector' refers to unincorporated enterprises below a size or registration threshold; but the 'Informal Economy' is broader — it covers all workers without social protection, including informal contract workers employed inside formally registered (organised) enterprises. Option C is the most tempting wrong answer but collapses both concepts into a firm-registration criterion, missing that formal firms can also employ informal workers.
